questions.question: What are RESTful routes in Rails?
questions.title: RESTful Routes in Rails
questions.direct_answer: RESTful routes map the HTTP verbs (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE) to CRUD actions on a resource, so the same URL does different things by verb: GET /posts (index, list), POST /posts (create), GET /posts/:id (show), PATCH /posts/:id (update), DELETE /posts/:id (destroy). Rails gives you all of them with resources :posts in routes.rb, which generates the 7 standard routes and path helpers (posts_path, post_path(id)). REST keeps your API predictable: a resource, its URL, and the verb tell you the action. Nested resources (resources :posts do resources :comments end) give /posts/:post_id/comments for a child collection.

interviewer_intent.testing: Whether you know resources :posts gives the 7 CRUD routes, the verb+URL+action mapping, and the path helpers (posts_path).
interviewer_intent.common_mistake: Hand-writing each route when resources :posts generates them, or using non-REST URLs (/list_posts, /create_post).
interviewer_intent.to_stand_out: resources :posts gives the 7 CRUD routes: GET /posts (index), POST /posts (create), GET /posts/:id (show), PATCH /posts/:id (update), DELETE /posts/:id (destroy). Predictable URLs + verbs.

sections.title: Resources and the 7 Routes
sections.content: RESTful routes map the HTTP verbs (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE) to CRUD actions on a resource, so the same URL does different things by verb: GET slash posts (index, list), POST slash posts (create), GET slash posts slash id (show), PATCH slash posts slash id (update), DELETE slash posts slash id (destroy). Rails gives you all of them with resources posts in routes.rb, which generates the 7 standard routes and path helpers (posts_path, post_path of id). REST keeps your API predictable: a resource, its URL, and the verb tell you the action. Nested resources — resources posts do resources comments end — give slash posts slash post_id slash comments for a child collection.

sections.title: resources :posts -> 7 Routes
sections.content:
One line generates the 7 CRUD routes with path helpers.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  R[resources :posts] --> G[GET /posts: index]
  R --> P[POST /posts: create]
  R --> S[GET /posts/:id: show]
  R --> U[PATCH /posts/:id: update]
  R --> D[DELETE /posts/:id: destroy]
```

sections.title: RESTful routes
sections.content:
```ruby
# config/routes.rb
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  resources :posts     # generates all 7 routes below
end

# The 7 routes `resources :posts` creates:
#   Verb     URL              Action    Helper
#   GET      /posts           index     posts_path
#   GET      /posts/new       new       new_post_path
#   POST     /posts           create    posts_path
#   GET      /posts/:id       show      post_path(@post)
#   GET      /posts/:id/edit  edit      edit_post_path(@post)
#   PATCH    /posts/:id       update    post_path(@post)
#   DELETE   /posts/:id       destroy   post_path(@post)

# Nested resource (a post's comments):
Rails.application.routes.draw do
  resources :posts do
    resources :comments   # /posts/:post_id/comments
  end
end
```

sections.title: Common Mistakes
items: Hand-writing each route when resources :posts generates them all.
Using non-REST URLs (/list_posts, /create_post) — break the convention.
Deep nesting (/posts/:p/comments/:c/replies/:r) — shallow nesting reads better.

sections.title: Key Takeaways
items: REST maps verbs to CRUD: GET (read), POST (create), PATCH (update), DELETE (remove).
resources :posts generates the 7 standard routes and path helpers.
Same URL, different verb = different action (/posts POST vs GET).
Path helpers: posts_path, post_path(@post), new_post_path, edit_post_path.
